However, they can also nudge players into equipping gear that may actually be worse for their specific build.[/p][p]Meanwhile, experienced players often see flat scoring systems as misleading and tend to ignore them altogether. Ultimately, we’d rather players evaluate gear based on what it actually [i]does[/i], the stats, the affixes, the synergy with their build, rather than judge on a single abstract number.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Character Progression & More obtainable skills in the story[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Due to the randomness, it can be frustrating for new players to progress through the story without discovering new skills. This often makes the experience feel dry, especially during the early levels when players are still exploring the game's systems and want to experiment.[/p][p][/p][p]To address this, players will be guaranteed to find skill Fragments at key moments in the story, typically after major quests, similar to how the [i]Gift of the Eternal[/i] is awarded.[/p][p][/p][p]We've previously discussed our goal of adding more "wow" moments to the player's progression, and we hope this change contributes to that experience.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Prologue & Onboarding[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Since Early Access launched, we’ve been going through a ton of feedback, and one thing that came up a lot is the prologue and the initial walk through Montescail.
[/p][p]Some of you liked being able to try out different classes early on (which is awesome), but overall, we’ve heard that the prologue felt just too long for many of our players. The [i]constant [/i]voice-over and up to 20 minutes of dialogue were often mentioned as overwhelming.[/p][p][/p][p]During that time, the player is basically unkillable, one-shotting everything, and loot is disabled for story purpose. While it’s not a big issue, when it stretches out for that long, it just isn't [i]fun[/i].[/p][p][/p][p][b]That’s why we’re already working on reducing the length of the prologue.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Another major point of feedback concerns the very first walk through the City of Montescail.[/p][p][/p][p]When players arrive in the City for the first time, they’re required to walk through the City while listening to dialogue before reaching the next quest point. Although our goal was to introduce the City in an immersive way, we now understand that this part feels tedious and not engaging.[/p][p][/p][p][b]As a result, we’ve decided to completely remove that initial walk.[/b][/p][h3][b]
New Modifiers[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Alongside the new skills we’ve been working on, we’d like to introduce a total of 9 modifiers.[/p][p][/p][p]Some of these new modifiers are a bit special as each one is [i]unique to a specific class[/i].[/p][p]They're designed to complement each class’s core identity and should open to more interesting build paths, making theorycrafting more flexible.[/p][p][/p][p]If you're curious, we shared a preview of these new modifiers on our Discord.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]To learn more about the Tracker update:[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/544486109101425001"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/498323476114834553"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/498325386812198381"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/498325386812195979"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/498324752822173944"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2][b]Looking ahead[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]We really hope you’ll like these changes and are eager to learn more about all these future features and changes.[/p][p]We are committed to keeping you informed as we implement these updates and are actively working to ensure that these changes are positive for both new and experienced players.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Sharing Your Experience[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We want to know how you get on with the [i]Nurõrgartt [/i]update, join us on Discord.[/p][p]And with that, we’ll catch you next time.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Loot Filter & Death Recap
notes.content:
[p]Hello Dragon hunters,[/p][p][/p][p]There is tons of new content throughout the Tracker update, and this past month showed off [i]some[/i] you can expect this summer:[/p][list][*][p][b]New Class:[/b]  The Tracker[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Biome[/b]: [i]Erde-nòr[/i][/p][/*][*][p][b]New Skills[/b]: For each class[/p][/*][*][p][b]New City feature:[/b] The Draconic Atlas[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Endgame feature: [/b]The[b] [/b]Draconic Tarot[/p][/*][/list][p]That said, there's more to come, and we haven't shared everything yet.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/f5d5f98af906678b89a51f22dac321f0ae936199.png"][/img][/p][p]In today’s post, we want to talk a bit about the [b]Quality of Life improvements[/b] we’ve been working on over the past few weeks, including some that have been highly requested since the start of Early Access.[/p][p][/p][p]Let's take a look![img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/38f58e18deaf59c1a8cfa7e7aed49897b6060043.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Loot Filter is on it’s way[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]As one of the most hotly requested features since the start of Early Access, we started working on a Loot Filter a few weeks ago, and we’re excited to show you how it looks.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/4446fef9f288eae761962336f1dfddc8518e62fc.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b2b207c1d8428c0b86d00ad5a91acc243f264ad1.png"][/img][i]Please note: This feature is still work in progress[/i][/p][p][/p][p]You’ll be able to:[/p][list][*][p]Create templates, set rules, and sort them by priority[/p][/*][*][p]Hide, display, or highlight / embelish specific types of items (give them different color)[/p][/*][/list][p]You’ll also have the option to automatically [b]convert items[/b] to the Grand Benedictor and/or Dark Merchant.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/92a3c1c9e646e3afc50bd4ea7f5e82e14ff6e1d2.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Rename your templates / layouts[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We’re also adding a way to [b]rename your templates / layouts[/b] for the Loot Filter, and the Arsenal.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/dbbf114adb2db633d7d5b198222788598baa9c10.gif"][/img][i]Please note: This feature is still work in progress[/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c3fa47384da910a3794e4f5d0b9d843b7e507a31.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Death Recap[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Death happens fast, and you don't always know what happened.
That’s something we’re aiming to improve with the introduction of the Death Recap.[/p][p]This new feature is meant to help interpret what caused you to die. Specifically, when there are a lot of enemies or chaotic fights. Our main goal is to help players answer questions like:[/p][p][/p][p][i]“What type of damage killed me?”[/i] - [i]“Which enemies are the most threatening?”[/i][/p][p][/p][p]This way, you will be able to adapt and improve for the next encounter.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/23feac903b054535b5d2ddf8075f32b9caa18eb2.gif"][/img][i]Please note: This feature is still work in progress[/i][/p][p][/p][p][b]How does it works?[/b][/p][p]Upon a character's death, you can see the [b]Death Log[/b], a recap providing valuable insights up to the last moments of combat.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Timeline[/b][/p][p]You'll be able to view the [b]timeline[/b] of events across the last few seconds with a [i]moment-by-moment[/i] view of damage taken, showing:[/p][list][*][p]Health, Shield[/p][/*][*][p]The types of damage received  Physical, Fire, Ice, Toxic, and Electric[/p][/*][*][p]Whether the damage was a direct hit or a DoT (damage over time), and the source[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][b]Expendable window[/b][/p][p]Clicking on the window expands the Death Recap to display more specific information, including:[/p][list][*][p]The total amount of damage taken,[/p][/*][*][p]The types of damage received, along with the percentage of each type[/p][/*][*][p]The total hits taken[/p][/*][*][p]The number of sources of damage[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/bd676427cd108583dd3902697014a0aec36b1442.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Info Box (in character selection)[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]When you start creating multiple characters, especially those of the same class, it can get difficult to remember which one has which build. That’s why we’re adding an [b]Info Box[/b] that displays useful info, the most important being the [b]character [/b]and [b]Wyrmling’s active skills[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/02bb92278c3591699b3fe4f6268a0a75162f1f08.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]We take your feedback into account[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]As usual, things [i]may[/i] evolve and we’re eager to see your feedback as we continue to work alongside the community. We hope this teaser was enough to hold you over until the release of the [i]Erde-nòr [/i]update.[/p][p]Of course, if you have any questions about these new features, don’t hesitate to ask them right here in the comments![/p][p][/p][p]Don’t forget to join our [b]Discord[/b] to be a part of our community, ask questions to the developers directly.[/p][p]See you soon and until next time. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: New Skills Preview
notes.content:
[p]Hey Dragon hunters,[/p][p]Our second major update introduces [b]2 skills for each character[/b] and a total of [b]17 skills for the Tracker[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/3798bd89b13d3dc0de8cad1e6977c3390da59878.png"][/img][/p][p]In this Dev Blog, we’ll break down all these new skills and share 2 more [b]Tracker[/b] abilities, in the continuity of our recent Dev Blog introducing [b]Qara Tani[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]If you haven’t read that one yet, we recommend checking it out here: [dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/544486109101425001"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]For this patch, our main focus was adding ranged basic ability for the Knight, Oracle, Barbarian, along with defensive abilities tailored to balance their weak spots and emphasize on their respective playstyles.[/p][p]One of our long-term goals is to expand build options for every character, so whether you prefer ranged, melee, burst, defense builds, we’d like to give our players enough choices to fit your playstyle.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Upcoming skills[/b][/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/bead27dc1e7e8a388ad4ec88768a1908884e8624.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Lothair De Montdragon - The Knight[/b][/h3][p]
These new skills aim to help Lothair to stay safe by having ranged basic attack but also a defensive ability that heals allies and deals damage, all while letting him move freely.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Defensive Blow[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Lothair strikes with his shield, dealing physical damage based on his Block stat. Like every basic skill, an enemy hit by the ability generates Energy.[/p][p]Also, worth pointing out: [i]Defensive Blow[/i] counts as both a melee hit and a projectile.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/607a83b947b0377380f374df307c8f8de0a7f351.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/bdacd9d16f685199ba58f13f5678e174e7da12b3.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/10e4dde7d14d17ba6dff372342b65b8e6fe8a445.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Heaven’s Hope[/b][/h3][p]Lothair invokes a burning light. healing nearby allies over time and dealing fire damage to enemies in the area each second.[/p][p]He can move freely while it’s active and cast other abilities, such as [i]Brave Charge and Intense Propulsion, [/i]without interrupting [i]Heaven’s Hope, [/i]and vice versa.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/9f59ae3d5308d759f51110a69e26d47c6765c079.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c74127a448d5635d9022efcc63f94c91129b629d.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7146229b3e26bfff72f2f735e347749344d0ad49.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/ba9fca1bcb79ed69cff98a55e850560412b842bb.png"][/img][b]Electrane - The Oracle[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Electrane is great at keeping enemies afar with her control tools and teleports. The last patch focused on her ability to control the battlefield, this time we’re leaning more into spacing tools and introducing an alternative to her shield that lets her buy time while still dealing damage. [/p][p][i]Pythoderkon’s Premonition[/i] helps Electrane setup bursts, whether by giving her time for cooldowns to be up or teleporting safely out of danger.[/p][p] [/p][h3][b]Energy Projection[/b] [/h3][p]Fires a psychic projectile that pierces enemies, dealing physical damage, and generating Energy on-hit. Every third shot deals bonus damage.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Vision:[/b] Directly launch the third projectile.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/0e9d1045c95865d9c0e1abc472de601cabc4d854.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d6488346a5636f1ab1c354f6390d70bd80df3990.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/0675ee2487b777bc91a4478e5676c56affa94a49.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Pythoderkon’s Premonition[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Electrane zaps nearby enemies, dealing electric damage over time and becomes Unstoppable, gaining massive resistance but becoming immobilized for a short duration.[/p][p][/p][p][b] Vision: [/b]Heals herself every second for the duration.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/18cdb76577e7da29c62b2a2e28a311abded01dc7.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/0354f9336233846c0f8c4da9bdc47e2248d05d25.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/9cfaadf8de263f6342f32a0c3ad10e30a992d759.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b23d67799c0056d324b03eacc41d7d0d96ee9bee.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Rurik Haraldson - The Barbarian[/b][/h3][p]
This patch introduces [i]Unleash Fury[/i], a new skill that boosts Thorn damage and adds some defensive perks, which is pretty rare. The new basic skill [i]Spear of Ice [/i]give Rurik more options at range, supporting mid-range builds[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Spear of Ice[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Ryrik launches a spear in the target direction, dealing ice damage and piercing enemies. Each enemy hit generates Energy.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/de627b0230258cd0172a21950dd30acb68ee6af5.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/4c8466d1686cbe1518a9d55250fd4be118749af9.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/74e2355b11959817a9ee87b72d4ac747b774a603.png"][/img][/p][h3]
[b]Unleashed Fury[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Rurik slams his arm down, dealing physical damage to all enemies struck within the area, scaling with Attack and Thorn. On cast, Rurik gains a temporary boost to Armor and Thorns for a short time.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/f5272c42c91ba821ef8894489c68958c9cb02bd7.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/35c5e369da2431e758919398293dc540299fe59e.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/4b1a74197ae86b482d92a36db19a83d63b8b136a.png"][/img] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/242d6945f223d0382519d7bba19ceea5cbb928a9.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Qara Tani, The Tracker[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We would also like to take the opportunity to show you more of the Tracker’s skills.[/p][p]Many of you know from the prologue that she has [i]Ricochet Shot[/i], a ranged ability that generates Energy. This DevBlog introduces [i]Windbreaker[/i];  a melee basic ability.[/p][h3]
[b]Windbreaker[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Qara Tani strikes the nearest enemy, dashing forward if out of reach. Each hit generates Energy, with the third hit dealing bonus damage and marking the enemies..[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/0dcb5fd8e35d33ed0cd65674ec4b59735bdb7450.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/bbef1f72e8ee971bb19333ef016b532cf0879190.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/ca59d34bcbd405e5b502699948e0c22e700c6671.png"][/img]                       [/p][p][/p][h3][b]Blinding Retreat[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Qara Tani quickly retreats and deploys a trap that slows enemies within the area. After a few seconds, it detonates, poisoning and marking all enemies caught in the blast.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/8169936741412535f87015f57dc2f5bee1e50161.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/af1c38429bcc1d1b65b1c3d7b761c352398e9b42.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/e5e3da910b6a3c1d702b2c261013f085a05f6937.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]That’s it for today![/b][/h2][p][/p][p]This wraps up our Dev Blog on the new skills coming with the [i]Erde-nòr[/i] update. While you wait, feel free to start theorycrafting, we’ll be keeping an eye on your ideas![/p][p][/p][p]If you’re not on our Discord yet, we’d love to have you join us.[/p][p]We share regular updates there, and we recently shared the results of the [b]Sneak Peek -Founder Pack 3 for the Tracker[/b] and shared our work on a long-awaited community feature: [b]the loot filter[/b]![/p][p][/p][p]See you next week![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Community Spotlight #2
notes.content:
[p]Hey Dragon hunters! Welcome to our second Community Spotlight![/p][p][/p][p]It’s been a little over a month since we released our first major update, and we really enjoy seeing how you receive these changes, especially regarding the progression, combat feel, and the new City features.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/78b3f9af4bd4117c45e249b8535a438d69748c98.png"][/img][/p][p]The new skills sparked a lot of interest, so we thought this would be a great time to highlight some of the builds that are making use of them, along with a few creative ones.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/174396bf037c6a2d1546e04a158f6fdd29c77999.png"][/img][/p][h3]Dragonkin: The Banished data collection sheet (by Mumpitz)[/h3][p]Before we get into some of our favorite builds from the community, we want to give a quick shoutout to Mumpitz, one of the most active members on our Discord, who’s been putting together a data sheet for [i]Dragonkin: The Banished[/i] to help the community.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Check it out:[/b] [url="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15U6hd-wI37gc-_R5weQc8APEJ8R4QbpWJBlxdvFAhAk/edit?gid=0#gid=0"]Dragonkin: The Banished date collection sheet[/url][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7461e6e07fad61afda994a4c0b58772f2b9de070.png"][/img][/p][p]Now, let’s take a look at your builds![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/97bc199ce6cee0e9123b8d05e5ffdce947cb8589.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Community Builds[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We love seeing how players approach the Ancestral Grid in different ways, especially when new skills shake things up. So, here are a few community builds that caught our attention this patch.[/p][p][/p][h3] Ice Cyclone – A Starter-Friendly Oracle Build (from Mumpitz)[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/20b2e5c9d3a0b6e1c0559058e4f1f6a7dd5b065d.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b993a71f351d035277ded72f61cbf5eb05b81fb4.gif"][/img][/p][p]Once again, Mumpitz delivers a very detailed build![/p][p]This time sharing us a Starter-friendly Ice Cyclone build for the Oracle using [b]Psychokinesis[/b] and [b]Writhing Cyclone[/b][i] [/i]to deal massive amounts of damage. [/p][p][/p][p]Here their reasoning behind the build:[/p][quote][p][i]“My goal was to make use of new skill Psychokinesis as well as the new wyrmling skill Frigid Wind that supports damage over time skills, which fits to Writhing Cyclone. So the target skills were selected. Anything else just evolved naturally on the journey.”[/i][/p][/quote][p][/p][p]If you’re interested, we highly recommend checking the full guide on Discord.[/p][p]You’ll find gear tips, stat priorities, and more.[/p][p][/p][p][url="https://discord.com/channels/1153987418618351616/1381061159888748594" style="button"]Check the full guide[/url][/p][p][/p][h3]Toxic Whirlwind - A Gold Farming Barbarian Build (from hr31)[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/24c8ad1b8641098c312f7c8be295bf72e6bd9094.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/6333200ec0ea9e134aba9199a4d0fbc511100c21.gif"][/img][/p][p]Barbarian [b]Whirlwind [/b]certainly is one, if not, the most popular build for the Barbarian. That said, hr31 [i]slightly[/i] revisits the classic [b]Whirlwind[/b] Barbarian.[/p][p]One of the key additions is the use of the [b]Ancestral Totem[/b] introduced in the last update.
Its area-of-effect damage and reliable attack bonus naturally complement the build.[/p][p][/p][p] A few words from hr31 on their approach:[/p][quote][p][i]“After trying out three classes, I concluded that Whirlwind offers the fastest movement, including when defeating monsters. I hadn't been using the Toxic Wyrmling before, but after the patch update, I started utilizing it. Moving forward, I plan to make use of lightning.”[/i][/p][/quote][p][/p][p]It’s worth noting that while Electric Wyrmling skills offer higher raw damage, the Toxic Wyrmling provides better sustain and energy regeneration, giving the Barbarian more resilience.[/p][p]The intent with that build is pretty clear: complete quests and activities such as Dungeon Purification as efficiently as possible. With an itemization focused on [b]+1,871% bonus gold gain[/b], this build wants to get golds![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/f0c5af6f651c91356655f62ec253b64d3ae027dd.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]  [url="https://discord.com/channels/1153987418618351616/1385849628448002118" style="button"]Check the full guide[/url][/p][p][/p][h3]Electric Axe of Toriel + Meteoric Projection Barbarian Build (by Bunzine)[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/5258e41f01c0385fb9730044467aa3050ed1183e.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7ef5444ae632de8dbcb7da4cfbf5604029ba0ca2.gif"][/img][/p][p]Bunzine proves there's still plenty of room to explore with the Barbarian.[/p][p]This build centers around [b]Axes of Toriel[/b] as the main skill, and uses [b]Meteoric Projection[/b] to deal massive damage by stacking projectile modifiers.[/p][p][/p][p]In their own words:[/p][quote][p][i]“This build focuses on using Axes of Toriel and Ultimate Meteoric Projection to quickly clear dungeons and defeat bosses. Axes of Toriel are thrown forward and return like boomerangs, dealing damage twice — once on the way out and once on the way back. Meteoric Projection is your ultimate skill, dealing high AoE damage.[/i][/p][p]In principle, this can be done with any wyrmling. However, you will need to adjust everything to match that wyrmling’s damage (including gear) and use different Wyrmling skills and attributes. The most important requirement is that you have the Dragon Wisdom (6) talent."[/p][/quote][p][/p][p][url="https://discord.com/channels/1153987418618351616/1387563369091039232" style="button"]Check the full guide[/url][/p][p][/p][h3]Electric Scarlet Thrust – A Wyrmling Focused Knight Build[/h3][h3](by MorkeX)[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/67add270e2960565d148818daa34b49041cab1bb.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/40bd978b91d61860e86b0a9e1591998caed314bc.gif"][/img][/p][p]MorkeX surprised us with a clever Knight build that relies on Wyrmling skills to deal damage instead of character skills.[/p][p][/p][p]Here’s the core concept explained by MorkeX:[/p][quote][p][i]“No energy or fuel consumption, one-button gameplay, excellent tankiness, high armor stats, medium clear speed, prone to missing mobs, RNG-dependent damage (since it relies on chance-based triggers) – perfect for fun-seeking players! It can breeze through all in-game content with ease.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][i]In this build, Wyrmling skills trigger randomly, so maximizing their proc rate was crucial (they’re the main damage source). Trigger chance directly dictates one dimension of attack frequency, which in turn relies on basic attack speed. These two factors form the final damage frequency. Projectile Tag Synergy: Dragon skills carry the "projectile" tag, so boosting projectile count not only amps up damage but also improves AOE coverage. then squeezed out damage potential through gear, talents, and Ancestral Fragments."[/i][/p][/quote][p][/p][p]The approach leans into synergy between [b]basic attacks[/b] and [b]projectile-triggered effects[/b], making it both sustainable and surprisingly strong.[/p][p]
For talents, MorkeX prioritized defense and survivability by maxing out [b]Armor of the Eternal[/b] and [b]Divine Avatar[/b] as early as possible, making the build extremely tanky while still dealing solid damage.[/p][p][/p][p][url="https://discord.com/channels/1153987418618351616/1387785548227280936" style="button"]Read the full guide[/url][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/373701728070d725470c73a182db5bc635218427.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Community Events[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]As you probably already know, we love running community events on our Discord and sharing sneak peeks behind the scenes.[/p][p][/p][p]Recently, we hosted [b]Choose the Next Sneak Peek! – Founder Pack 3[/b], and with your votes, we revealed the [i]Dracomondus Priestess armor[/i] for the Oracle.[/p][p]Since you seemed to enjoy that event, we’d like to do it again, this time, for the [b]Tracker[/b]![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d59e27f39490eabf5050bfe4c5e269abe643e691.png"][/img][/p][h3]Event Duration:[/h3][p]From [b]NOW[/b] until [b]Tuesday, July 1, 2025[/b][/p][p][/p][h3]What’s this about?[/h3][p][/p][p]We’ve got 3 unique Tracker customization options, and we want you to decide which one we reveal next week on our Discord server. Cast your vote for option 1, 2, or 3![/p][p][/p][p]To help you decide, here’s a little flavor behind each look:[/p][olist][*][p][i]“An outfit made from Dragonkin that lets you move among them without raising suspicion.”[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]“Armor worn by the ultimate defenders of the lost civilization deep in the jungles of Ja’Ksara.”[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]“Legends say stray spirits from the Mangerika Springs seek new hosts...”[/i][/p][p][/p][/*][/olist][p]The customization with the [b]most votes will be featured[/b] in our upcoming sneak peek.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/e132010515aa8e86f68aae87e026c6e903fe19c5.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Votes started already![/i][/p][p][/p][h3][b]What’s To Come[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We're still continuing our work on bug fixing the issues you have brought to us. We are also listening to your feedback so far and will be implementing some changes![/p][p][/p][p]We know many of you are wondering which areas we’re focusing on for the next update, and we want to let you know that a Dev Blog is planned in the coming weeks to go over [b]the major points we are working on and address.[/b][/p][p]We ask for a bit of patience as it takes time to wrap it all up properly, but in the meantime, here’s a quick look at a few key things we’d like to talk about:[/p][list][*][p][b]Prologue & Onboarding[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Overall progression (loot adjustment)[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Getting one-shot out of nowhere & Death penalty[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]And more...[/b][/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3][b]That's it for today[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Feel free to share more of your builds, which might be featured in a future community spotlight! And as always, if you encounter any bugs, join our Discord server to report them.[/p][p][/p][p]See you soon![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png"][/img] [/p]

notes.title: Introducing the Draconic Tarot & Atlas
notes.content:
[p]Hey Dragon hunters,[/p][p][/p][p]After last week’s DevBlog giving a first look at the highly anticipated Tracker, this time we’re back but to show other features we’ve been quietly working on, yet crucial in sharpening the endgame loop of Dragonkin: The Banished.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/ddc729463959a66f192ac6543c1958f400da5420.png"][/img][/p][p]Expect these changes to come as part of the [i]Erde-nòr[/i] update![img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d3248e486e1e9b9cf192fbcfa2f0ff0a14ab9759.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Introducing the Draconic Tarot[/b][/h3][p]As of now, Chaos Hunts already offer a [i]fair [/i]amount of flexibility, you can choose how long they are, where they take place, the final enemy, and the activity.[/p][p][/p][p]But one thing has always been a bit of a pain: [b]modifiers[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Right now, modifiers are randomly set once the hunt begins. If you didn't get the modifiers you were [i]hoping[/i] for, you'd have to quit and start over. Which, we understand, can be quite tedious.[/p][p][/p][p][b]That’s why we’re going to introduce the Draconic Tarot in our next update,[/b] designed to give you more control over the [i]Chaos Hunts[/i] and tailor your experience.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/05dda44b0e8f78813b2077a98478d6948a0cf888.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]How does it works?[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]In the [i]Chaos Hunts[/i] tab on the Hunting Board, you'll be able to select one or multiple [i]Fate Cards[/i].[/p][p]
Each of them grants:[/p][list][*][p]Positive modifier(s) and / or increased loot quality[/p][/*][*][p]Negative set of modifiers[/p][/*][/list][p]Some [i]Fate Cards[/i] can also have:[/p][list][*][p]Neutral modifiers (e.g. increased critical rate and damage for both you and enemies) [/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/56ccbf631573261bb4b48732c7db24ea09c72c54.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/57d0a4ea4558bd019c5d7f22a5337610d8bd0c74.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]There are [b]15[/b] [i]Fate Cards[/i] total and you can stack them up to 11 Fate Cards [i](this number may change in the future)[/i], making your [i]Chaos Hunt[/i] more challenging but increasing Loot Quality for those willing to take the challenge.[/p][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p][i]As a reminder, Loot Quality affects your chances of obtaining higher rarity items when a drop occurs. It doesn't increase the overall drop rate, but rather improves the likelihood that dropped items will be of higher rarity.[/i][/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p]Some of you may notice that we're being more transparent with the stats.[/p][p]
That’s why, in the future, we’ll try to display more percentages in our tooltips to give you a better understanding of the odds, even though it sometimes requires making technical or localization choices that demand extra work.[/p][p]
We hope that this new addition will not only provide an [i]extra [/i]challenge for hardcore players but make the [b]Chaos Hunts [/b]more [i]fun![/i][/p][p][/p][p][b]Please note that this system still is work in progress![/b][/p][p]As such, the visuals of the UI, Fate Cards, modifiers, requirements, and limitations are subject to change.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/4603a53537db2ba08b274585b9e7f443904c5923.png"][/img][/p][p]Now, let’s take a look at a new service coming to the City of Montescail: the [b]Draconic Atlas[/b].[/p][p]This new service can be unlocked in the [i]Old Town[/i]. There you’ll be able to visit the librarian.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d95598b444fcbfbb78abb854d734ce09208d1d45.png"][/img][/p][p]The [b]Draconic Atlas[/b] is designed to help you learn more about the enemies you encountered during your hunts, while also providing passive bonuses that apply to all characters tied to the same City.[/p][h3]
[b]How does it works?[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]The Draconic Atlas automatically logs enemies you’ve defeated and gradually unlocks information about them. As usual, progress is shared across all characters tied to the City.[/p][p][/p][p]If you’ve already defeated enemies before unlocking the Atlas, they’ll be counted, meaning the Atlas is retroactive! So you don’t have to worry about unlocking it as soon as possible.[/p][p][/p][p]Additionally, each time an enemy’s analysis rank increases, it grants experience to your City, with bosses granting even more experience than regular enemies.[/p][p][/p][p]Enemies in the Atlas appear in one of [b]2 states[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Unknown[/b][/p][p]You haven’t encountered this enemy yet, thus no entry appears in the Atlas
[/p][/*][*][p][b]Encountered[/b][/p][p]You’ve defeated this enemy at least once, and its name and model become visible[/p][/*][/list][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/936da5acde98df2268985ea4f35a0c3043a18ce8.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Enemy Analysis[/b][/p][p]Once an enemy is marked as [i]Encountered[/i], you can increase its analysis rank (Bronze > Silver > Gold) by defeating more of that enemy. Each rank unlocks a permanent damage bonus against it.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Biome Completion[/b][/p][p]By [i]Encountering [/i][b]ALL [/b]enemies of a biome and increasing their rank  (Bronze > Silver > Gold) unlock a permanent elemental resistance bonus.[/p][p][b]Note:[/b] These bonuses from each tier are cumulative, and apply to all characters in the City.[/p][p][/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/0b41f02618021be93668da03450086662e5bcba7.png"][/img][/h3][h3][b]Founder Pack 3 Preview[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We recently ran the [b]"Choose the Next Sneak Peek!"[/b] event on Discord to let the community decide which preview we should reveal from the upcoming Customization Pack.[/p][p][/p][p]The event has now concluded, and the community has spoken! The [b]Oracle [/b]was chosen![/p][p][/p][p]Take a look at the [b]Dracomondus Priestess armour[/b] for the Oracle, designed by [i]Agathe Dhondt[/i].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c161feabb7331320bb822614ba52b4c52de3871d.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b87d7ac9b1998fe09955cdd0d6aeb0f8b0649416.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Share your builds on Discord![/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We want to see the creative builds you're running and the ideas you've come up with.
Also, next week, we would like to highlight some of our favorites in a Community Spotlight.[/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/af31940ba82ab37adfd53815b88c61c1124a4180.png"][/img][/h3][p][/p][h3][b]That’s it for today![/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We often share previews of what we’re working on and host events, so if you’re interested, feel free to join us on our Discord server![/p][p][/p][p]See you next week! [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Meet Qara Tani, the Tracker
notes.content:
[p]Hey Dragon hunters,   

We know you've been eager to learn more about the Tracker, so here we are with a new DevBlog! As a reminder, she is coming with the 2nd major [i]Dragonkin: The Banished update[/i]. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/464db0a9545401d4b0d14fe7779f243a2cdb5b42.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We're excited to give you a proper look at her! She will be launching with a [b]total of 17 skills[/b] and today we’ll showcase [b]3[/b] of them that you didn't see in the Prologue.[/p][p]
Let’s take a look![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/242d6945f223d0382519d7bba19ceea5cbb928a9.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Qara Tani, The Tracker[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][i]As a Tracker, she uses the deadly techniques of archery and hand-on-hand combat learnt from her clan, enhanced by her knowledge of poisonous plants and fauna.[/i][/p][p][i]She is able to wield all the martial techniques, ranging from formidable close-combat skills to powerful ranged attacks.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/6bc5d7541c165142b8ce589dfff6acf52033fc01.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Innate Ability: Targeting[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]When the Tracker hits an enemy with any ability, she applies a [b]Mark[/b].[/p][p]Enemies can have up to [b]4 Marks[/b] (subject to change). When activated, Qara Tani throws a knife at every marked enemy, consuming all [b]Marks[/b] on each target for a lethal burst attack.[/p][p]Enemies then take damage that scales with the number of [b]Marks[/b] applied to them and Qara Tani refunds energy for every enemy killed that way or if they had the maximum of [b]Marks (4)[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]The [b]green gauge[/b] displays how many enemies are currently marked. When full, Qara Tani can’t [b]Mark[/b] additional targets until some are cleared.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/6aef76fe99f9a6daea8e83eb017e050ba40e7f4d.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We wanted the Tracker passive to reflect Qara Tani's background as a disciplined hunter; someone who’s always watching, waiting, and preparing for the perfect strike. Targeting creates a flow of combat that lets her choose when to burst down an enemy or when to restore energy and follow up on her next target.[/p][h3]
[b]Gathered Gales[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Qara Tani charges her bow up to 2 seconds to increase Gathered Gales' damage and repels enemies hit by the projectile(s).[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7b1f746f02452d0b85b919b9a6c61a46e8b280d9.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/f8894579fdc0c3af6a89060bab40c95a4b864a10.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/da1d63aa58f98674894516ef6eab97c39421443f.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Dance of Daggers[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Qara Tani channels, throwing toxic daggers in all directions, hitting nearby enemies.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/4b819e27d164394f9fa93db8488994a55b672b4a.gif"][/img][/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/098836b0d936f6fccd91eaaf7b9600c7bc003691.gif"][/img][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/27c3dcd5c0a20657dec675ad55e85ec4332c85f5.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Noxious Star[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Qara Tani fires a large toxic projectile that ricochets off walls. If an enemy is affected by damage over time, Noxious Star deals additional damage.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c2dc0fb89e4f6560cfea68a4a2b1432d154b9b3d.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/5e743a4847bfe4694cf5ee16776bbf497fc6f88d.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/4a40b0417842653ab4c73d67e8c786f8e858a561.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]That’s it for today’s DevBlog![/b][/h3][p][/p][p]And that was a quick summary of what the Tracker can do and what you can expect from her when our 2nd major update drops. As per usual, things may change [i]slightly [/i]as we're still working on her. 

That Said, we'd like to ask:[/p][p]Which of the Tracker’s skills are you most excited about? We're genuinely curious to know your thoughts![/p][p]And of course, once she’s released, we’d love to get your feedback.[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks for following along and we hope you continue to enjoy [i]Dragonkin: The Banished[/i].[/p][p]Until next time![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Behind the Narrative & World Design of Erde-nòr
notes.content:
Hello Dragon hunters!

Today, we’re giving you a first look at a new biome coming to Dragonkin: The Banished: [i]Erde-nòr[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/0bc5137fd44669dc0b598961128a55d73a8a77ad.png[/img]

Being a volcano region, it definitely tells you a lot already: scorched volcanic wasteland where molten rivers, buried ruins, and the remains of a forgotten stronghold collide.

Of course, you’ll run into new [i]dragonkins[/i] you certainly want dead.

Also, as part of our ongoing effort to make Dragonkin: The Banished a better game each day, we want our DevBlogs to follow that same process and make them more interesting for our readers.

That’s why, we’d like to take you behind the scenes, by not just going to preview the new environments but also talk about the [b]“World & Narrative”[/b] design of our game, and the process behind creating the world of [i]Dragonkin[/i].

[h3][b]So, what exactly [i]Is[/i] World Design & Narrative Design?[/b][/h3]

Before we walk you through the upcoming biome, let’s take a moment to explain what we mean when we talk about “World Design” and “Narrative Design” and how these two concepts shape the player’s experience.

At first glance, they might seem like the same thing, but they serve different roles:
[list]
[*] [b]World Design[/b] focuses on the physical space: the design, the layout, traversal, landmarks, and how the world reacts to the player
[/list]
Meanwhile…
[list]
[*] [b]Narrative Design[/b] is about: the lore, emotional implications & triggers, motivations, context, and storytelling tools used to bring that world to life
[/list]
Both of these aspects work together to answer a few and varied questions:

[i]Where is the player? What are they doing or fighting? Why are they doing this? How is this communicated to the player?[/i]

One of the very first goals of the Narrative Design is to induce a narrative tension in the viewer through curiosity, suspense, and surprise. World Design then works in tandem to shape the environment and create the atmosphere.

That’s the kind of experience many games aim to create and [i]Dragonkin: The Banished[/i] isn’t an exception.

In this DevBlog, we’ll take a look at how these concepts apply in our game and specifically for that new biome: [i]Erde-nòr[/i].
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/53e586d7c3802cd48128639216bbc6acd7cb1b15.png[/img]
[h3][b]The Volcanic Plains of Koleos[/b][/h3]

This new zone is the first area you’ll step into when arriving in [i]Erde-nòr[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/e335bcfe70f17ef1f074f5187449952b87d43282.png[/img]

From the beginning, our goal in designing the Volcanic Plains of Koleos was clear: to create a zone that feels dangerous and unwelcoming (like most of our biomes, to be honest).

As players progress further into the region, a series of questions should naturally come to their mind: [i]Who made this place? Why are they here? And what are they hiding?[/i]

Here we try to spark the player’s curiosity and create a sense of mystery. We want the player to feel that something happened here… but not sure what, not yet…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/93dfad4cfa12d77116a259769f226cf00ba0d3af.png[/img]

The answer to who made this place is pretty simple: [i]Saur Iknog[/i], the red dragon, or at least the one who gave it its current shape.

As to why the [i]dragonkins[/i] live here is explained by the fact this is the place where the cult began its efforts to bring [i]Saur Iknog[/i] back into the world, resulting in a corrupted land, now volatile, volcanic landscape players can now witness.

If you did the prologue, some of what’s waiting here might feel… familiar. That area is raining fireballs! Here comes the environmental hazards! Your [i]Wyrmling[/i] may protect you though!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/a31caa3bb86443703aa9e7375361d3ea52b54867.gif[/img]

And that, in essence, is the Narrative Design behind this region.

With that in mind, how does World Design help build that sense of pressure and danger? How do we communicate to the player through exploration and combat?

One way to create a sense of oppression, stifling, and ultimately kinda claustrophobic is by shifting how the environment and space feels over time.

The Volcanic Plains open with wide, and rather flat terrain, cracked earth, and burnt trees. There’s space to move and fight.

By venturing further, that feeling of openness gradually begins to fade. Lava flows start to segment the ground. What was once a broad plain breaks into isolated rock formations and ledges, with dragon-bone bridges spanning molten rivers that thread between them, just below the player’s feet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b09b2dc9d2a395c139293651902d1d6d2e6b53c9.png[/img]

Naturally, this type of design pushes us in a direction where we create more corridors and some tighter spaces.

However, such cramped environments aren't always enjoyable in ARPGs. For that reason, and to maintain a smooth gameplay experience, we made sure our players would also find larger, arena-like areas where the environment opens up again.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/cc923d2bade90d6faa9460bb1552fee41d70b83f.png[/img]

These larger spaces also are a perfect way for Narrative Design to use them through World Design. The cult’s presence becomes unmistakable here. Built structures, markings, and layout all work together to make these areas feel claimed and important. 

To reinforce that, we shift the visual tone, moving away from the red-orange lava palette into cooler purples and darker hues. It’s a subtle but deliberate signal to tell the player this place is different and worth visiting.

That way, we try to keep building the player's curiosity.

At last, players reach a stronghold entry in the volcano, where the real descent begins…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/bd8798fc169ff395a217f32fb5e234487ad827f1.png[/img]

[h3][b]Meet the Wyvern[/b][/h3]

One of the enemies you’ll run into in the Volcanic Plains of Koleos is the Wyvern, a pretty nasty mix between a dragon and a scorpion. 

The Wyvern’s core threat is its Tail Strike, a forward sting that embeds into the ground, leaving the Wyvern momentarily stuck and creating a temporary toxic AoE around the impact.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/8d2927265a8c35ecca040a2bf4bef2f6d963244b.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/62623a0e5678d3ed04626db43d6d877cb0ca9bbb.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/55109fe19c6953d80ab407f8d7b55ad87f4530a1.png[/img]
[h3][b]Resurgence Stronghold[/b][/h3]

Deep beneath the volcanic wastes lies a buried stronghold.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/3113b7a5862cb8e7dde5af35c57810bfac42dd57.png[/img]

World Design wise, the scale is much larger than the surface suggested, tall vertical shafts, layered platforms, and carved structures that go far deeper than expected.

That contrast is intentional. We wanted the reveal to feel surprising, like you’ve just stepped into something hidden and built for a very different purpose.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/da033398a0b67d390a184be00abf01ecf4f4487e.png[/img]

It’s now clear that the cult lives here and that’s why you’ll be able to find cult banners, prayer rooms, and dragonkins structures. But structurally, the fortress feels too refined to have been built by them alone. That disconnect is part of the Narrative Design intent: the stronghold doesn’t look like something the cult would have created..

Here, we want the player’s feelings to turn from curiosity to suspense and wonder: [i]“who built this?” turns into “what lies at the bottom?”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d95f5133535cd2c5537c3ec791e7ec8f3fd19a1f.png[/img]

While this zone [i]may[/i] look even more narrow than the previous one, you’ll find very large areas as you go deeper in the depths of the mountain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/1a60c17383da4eec6599aa937038534c90e00c4f.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/1227a8f984a4cdd218499815fbf366fb0ffd68d9.png[/img]

[h3][b]Meet the Dark Sorcerer[/b][/h3]

In the depths of the fortress corridors, you’ll undoubtedly cross paths with the Dark Sorcerer. 
Players who completed the prologue might recognize this ominous figure from the cinematic, but never had the opportunity to meet them in combat and see Its kit.

The Dark Sorcerer is a slow-moving, almost static, ranged enemy who uses elemental forces to damage and disrupt the player. His kit includes: An Ice Tempest, which conjures a protective ring of frost around him that blocks incoming projectiles Fireballs that fire in all directions; and a Lightning Beam,dealing electric damage at short charge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b3e42caf3298c7d69ae6b808f0e137a1f9dae736.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/f6074da8fd36b263e9eb706485aaaf70d5673278.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/066a9b9215de7491a9b1d0f409d14dab809d22e2.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/95f1e06f5ab2c42efa16d8568c43b725bf63a007.png[/img]
[h3][b]The Catacombs of Fire (Dungeon)[/b][/h3]

While delving in the dungeon, walls start to feel like ribs, everything feels… organic, darker, and closer, and strangely alive, as if you’ve slipped into the belly of a beast that shouldn’t exist.  All this to give a claustrophobic atmosphere. That’s definitely a hellish pit.

We’ve previously built up suspense, and now we want our players to be surprised and feel uncomfortable. We won’t tell you more about the Dungeon as we want you to explore it yourself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/ab7a738ac957064025ea12e9b6004c155cc9eb6c.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/84db3653919e61e81af1c261b9e259e3d734f001.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/938e5418b6939fce1a3f1e26140a3e33a009e052.gif[/img]

[h3][b]That’s it for today![/b][/h3]

That wraps up our DevBlog on the environments of [i]Erde-nòr[/i].

We hope you enjoyed this new approach, and we’d love to hear if you'd like more DevBlogs like this, giving you a closer look behind-the-scenes.

Next week, we’ll be talking about the major points we are already working on, as well as what we plan to address based on the feedback you've shared with us.

Of course, many of you are eager to learn more about the Tracker and specifically her kit and gimmick. In the meantime, we dropped a small sneak peek of one of her upcoming abilities (not shown in the prologue!) on our Discord, if you’d like to check!

We’ll be back soon with more updates, so stay tuned!

See you!
[url=https://discord.gg/WrCT2E5kG9][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Hotfix #1 Now Live!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We have just deployed a hotfix addressing some issues that were reported by our community, as well as various other bugs that have made their way into the game.

Please report any issues in the #bug-report channel on Discord.

Thanks for your patience, and we appreciate your continued support.

🐛[b]Bug Fixes[/b]

[i]Quests[/i]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where the [i]Protect the sapper[/i] objective in the endgame quest [i]Fire by fire[/i] couldn’t be completed
[/list]

[i]Crafting & Resources[/i]
[list]
[*] Fixed a crash that could occur when trying to reroll a modifier in a fragment at the Enchanter
[*] Fixed an issue with Divine ingredients not appearing in Gifts of the Eternal
[*] Fixed a bug where the Gift of the Eternal could be empty if the player died immediately after it spawned and could cause a crash
[/list]

[i]Enemies & Bosses[/i]
[list]
[*] Fixed the Green Mud Brute’s attack animation
[*] Fixed a bug where the Elementary Pseudopod had unintended constant shield regeneration
[*] Fixed an issue where the "Guardian" elite affix could stack infinitely, making enemies unkillable
[*] Adjusted visual effect for the new Frozen Elite Aura for better visual clarity
[/list]

[i]Fragments, Talents & Skills[/i]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with the Safe Distance modifier not being compatible with any skill
[*] Fixed the Ice Wyrmling Armor "Okaenos Cobalt Armour" that had a wrong talent
[*] Fixed an issue with the passive "Purification" that could trigger infinite crowd control effects under specific conditions
[/list]

[i]Miscellaneous[/i]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with Chaos Hunt parameters resetting to default in some scenarios
[*] Fixed an issue when using gamepad in City Customization view when the last focused element was not visible anymore
[*] Fixed an issue with the Delete Group Function which would not update properly the menu upon use
[*] Fixed an issue with the equipment Shared Chest where the 4th tab being hidden, making the  ANY items stored in that tab inaccessible
[/list]

[i]Localization[/i]
[list]
[*] Fixed a the name for the Sergeant of Fafnir enemy
[*] Fixed Alaric’s name displayed incorrectly in one of the story's quest
[*] Fixed an issue with an unwanted '+' sign before 'Damage dealt -10%, but +0.5% after finishing each wave in the Test of Will’s trial parameter in the Polish language
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes : Nurõrgartt
notes.content:
Hello Dragon hunters,

We are delighted to announce that Dragonkin's [b]First Major Update[/b], the [i][b]Nurõrgartt[/b][/i] patch has arrived!

[b]Please take a look at our Trailer:[/b]

[previewyoutube=sE8mhoDe8d0;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Oh! And Founder Pack 2 is here! Download it right here:[/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3594840/Dragonkin_The_Banished__Founder_Pack_2/

This patch introduces our 1st Major Update features and QoL updates requested by the community, along with several bug fixes.

As always, thank you to everyone who reported bugs and provided feedback to us!

Your support is crucial in shaping the future of Dragonkin and thanks to our fans, we’ve been able to go beyond the scope of what was in our initial roadmap.

A quick note regarding [b]Steam Deck[/b] support, [i]Dragonkin: The Banished[/i] is now officially playable! We’ll continue working toward full compatibility.

Patch notes will feature a [b][🔥][/b] emoji whenever the change is based on community feedback!

[h3][b][Highlights][/b][/h3]

[list]
    [*][b]6 new character skills[/b]
 [quote][i]2 for each class, including: the Knight, the Barbarian, and the Oracle.[/i][/quote][/list][list]
    [*][b]3 new Wyrmling skills[/b]
[quote][i]1 for the Ice Wyrmling and 2 for the Toxic Wyrmling.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]5 new Services in the City of Montescail[/b]
[quote][i]The Enchanter, The Memorialist, The Grand Benedictor, The Artificer, The Arsenal will be added to your city.

These are designed to give you more control around your itemization and builds.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]New Biome: [i]Nurõrgartt[/i][/b]
[quote][i]4 new levels in The Tundra and the Glacier environments.

New dungeon purification: The Ice Cavern.

New enemies, and bosses to discover.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]New endgame activity: Test of Will[/b]
[quote][i]In this mode, you'll face wave after wave of enemies while dealing with a mix of temporary buffs and debuffs, along with permanent bonuses that last throughout the run.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]New kind of reward: Gift of the Eternal[/b]
[quote][i]In our ongoing efforts to enhance player agency and reward progression, we'd like to introduce a new kind of reward: Gift of the Eternal.

Our goal with that new reward is to provide meaningful choices that respect your time and investment in the game. By allowing you to select rewards that align with your goals, we aim to enhance your gameplay experience and progression satisfaction.​[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]🔥New Storage Chest for Fragments[/b]
[quote][i]Many players have expressed frustration over the limited storage space for Fragments and we've heard you!

That’s why we introduce the Fragment chest! You’ll now find several Fragment chests scattered throughout the city, right alongside the familiar Equipment chest.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]15 new endgame hunts[/b]
[quote][i]New rewards to unlock on the Hunting Board for chaos hunts and for the Gift of the Eternal. Most Hunts happen in the new biome “Nurõrgartt”.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]🔥Progression & loot adjustments[/b]
[quote][i]Your feedback highlighted how the overall level progression, especially between levels 30 to 45 could feel underwhelming and unrewarding.

With this patch, we’ve taken the first steps to make leveling more satisfying by allowing players to obtain more interesting and high-rarity drops much earlier.

Our intention is to add more 'wow' moments for the player and make progression before max level feel exciting.

As such, [b]Divine & Draconic[/b] are now available starting at [b]level 1[/b] and [b]Mythical[/b] items drop from [b]level 30 instead of 45[/b]. The Gift of the Eternal, which can drop in the storyline and offers rarer items, should help reinforce that rewarding sense of progression.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]🔥Gameplay adjustment[/b]
[quote][i]This patch brings a wide wave of gameplay refinements aimed at making the core experience feel better. As such, we’ve touched many parts of the gameplay.

[b]Expect:[/b] increased enemy density, combat feel and responsiveness, loot visibility, difficulty adjustments, and of course overall skill balance.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]Quality of Life (QoL) & New options[/b]
[quote][i]We are adding in-game guides, features like level-up notifications, and improving tooltip readability.

[b]We also really want our players to customize their experience.[/b]

That’s why we’re adding plenty of settings for you to mess around with, such as high-contrast cursor, minimap transparency, camera distance, NPC and Enemy Highlight options, Colorblind mode and more.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*][b]Founder Pack 2 available[/b]
[quote][i][b]Dragonkin: The Banished. Founder Pack 2 contains:[/b]

6 exclusive pieces of equipment including a chest and a helmet for your heroes (2 per character)

6 exclusive visual effects allowing you to add a trail to your Wyrmling.

The exclusive pack “Day of the Dead Dragon” includes cosmetic elements for your city: statues, roofs, flags and pennants.[/i][/quote] [/list]

[h3][b][New Features][/b][/h3]

🎮[b]Gameplay[/b]
[list]
    [*]2 New skills for each class, including: the Knight, the Barbarian, and the Oracle

     [i]Knight[/i]

[list]
    [*]Compressed Air
[quote][i]Lothair pulls enemies inward and deals fire damage to them. While this ability has no cooldown and can be cast repeatedly, each use consumes Fuel.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*]Offensive Rempart
[quote][i]Lothair braces his shield in a chosen direction, channeling for a few seconds. During this time, he gains a huge chunk of armor and delivers continuous strikes in front of him while blocking incoming projectiles from the front.[/i][/quote] [/list]
     [i]Oracle[/i]

[list]
    [*]Psychokinesis
[quote][i]Electrane unleashes a shockwave that pulls enemies after a few seconds, briefly stunning them and dealing physical damage afterwards.

[b]Vision:[/b] Instantly pulls enemies and deals damage, allowing you to use it as a reaction spell.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*]Electric Wall
[quote][i]Electrane creates a passable electric wall. Enemies that pass through it are slowed and take damage over time while allies who pass through the wall gain increased movement speed.

[b]Vision:[/b] The wall increases in size, letting you cover larger areas and better control chokepoints.[/i][/quote] [/list]
     [i]Barbarian[/i]

[list]
    [*]Battering Ram
[quote][i]Rurik charges in a direction, steering his charge slightly. He deals ice damage to enemies along his path and at the end of the charge explodes in a blizzard of ice damage.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*]Ancestral Totem
[quote][i]Rurik summons a totem that periodically emits pulses of ice damage to nearby enemies. While active, it empowers the attacks of allies within its radius. The totem can draw enemy aggro and be destroyed.[/i][/quote] [/list]
    [*]3 New Wyrmling skills, including: 1 for the ice wyrmling and 2 for the Toxic Wyrmling

     [i]Ice Wyrmling[/i]

[list]
    [*]Frigid Wind
[quote][i]While the Wyrmling inflicts damage over time, has a chance of creating an area that  inflicts frostbite the enemies dealing damage over time.[/i][/quote] [/list]
     [i]Toxic Wyrmling[/i]

[list]
    [*]Voices of the swarm
[quote][i]While inflicting damage, the Wyrmling has a chance of creating a line of toxic spit across the screen.[/i][/quote] [/list][list]
    [*]Explosive sickness
[quote][i]While inflicting damage over time, the Wyrmling has a change of hitting the target with an explosion of toxic damage.[/i][/quote] [/list][/list] [list]
    [*]5 New Services added to the City of Montescail
